properties.summary: Incident Type: PIPELINE - NRC Report ID: 1332260 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: ADM AGRI-INDUSTRIES
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1332260
Incident Time: 2022-03-29 20:05:00
Nearest City: Windsor, CN
Location: 5550 MAPLEWOOD DR.
Incident Type: PIPELINE
Material: OIL, EDIBLE: VEGETABLE
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: ADM AGRI-INDUSTRIES
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 42.264494, -83.099586 (Approximated from premise)
Reported Spill Volume: 200 gallon
Report DescriptionEST. 200 GAL (~908 L) OF VEGETABLE OIL SPILLED FROM OPEN PIPE IN THE REFINERY WITH APPROX. 5 GAL (~ 23 L) IMPACTING THE DETROIT RIVER. LOCATION IN WATER IMPACTED IS NORTH OF THE SHIP DOCK, INSIDE THE BAY ON THE NE CORNER PRIOR TO THE LAND JUTTING WEST INTO D. RIVER. WEST OF THE ON-LAND TANK FARM. -CAUSE WAS WORKERS DOING WORK ON THE PIPE, VALVE WAS LEFT OPEN. PUMP KICKED ON AND CREW DIDN"T NOTICE VALVE WAS LEFT OPEN. PIPE HAS SINCE BEEN ISOLATED. NO FURTHER SPILLAGE OCCURRING. -GFL IS ALSO ON THIS CALL AND CONFIRMS THAT APPROX. 5 GAL IMPACTED THE RIVER AND INFORMS THAT ADM A-I CO. CREW DID A GOOD JOB OF CONTAINING SPILL. -2 ROLLS OF ABSORBENT PADS HAVE BEEN DEPLOYED. EACH ROLL IS APPROX. 75" LONG X 3" WIDE. PADS STILL IN PLACE ALONG THE EDGE OF THE SHORE/WATER AND BY THE OUTFALL AREA. SAYS MATERIAL IS TRAPPED IN THE BAY AREA CURRENTLY. NOT REALLY IMPACTING THE MAIN RIVER. -GFL HAS A VACTOR TRUCK ATTENDING (ETA 30 MIN.) TO BEGIN CLEAN UP BY FLUSHING AND VACUUMING UP THE SITE. WASTE COLLECTED WILL BE PROCESSED ONSITE AT THEIR WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY AND RE-INCORPORATED INTO THEIR PROCESSES. -DURATION OF CLEAN UP ESTIMATED AT 4 HRS. -FACILITY CRUSHES SOYBEAN AND CANOLA BEANS FOR OIL. -SAC ADVISED ADM A-I CO. & GFL TO ENSURE SAC IS UPDATED IF THE SITUATION DETERIORATES AND/OR WHEN THE CLEAN UP IS COMPLETED.

Report DescriptionPER REPORT: WE CURRENTLY HAVE A LEAK IN OUR STARBOARD AZIPULL DRIVE. THIS HAS BEEN REPORTED TO CLASS AND WE HAVE A CONDITION OF CLASS ISSUED. WE ARE SCHEDULED TO GO TO DRY DOCK AFTER HALIFAX FOR FURTHER INSPECTIONS / REPAIRS. THE CREW ONBOARD HAVE EXHAUSTED ALL EFFORTS TO INVESTIGATE THE ISSUE INCLUDING DIVERS IN OUR PREVIOUS PORT, PORT FURCHON USA. THE ENGINEERS ARE KEEPING A CLOSE EYE ON THE SITUATION AND ARE CURRENTLY REPORTING NO LOSS DESPITE 0.2BAR PRESSURE ON THE HEADER TANK. WE SUSPECT THIS MAY BE DUE TO THE CHANGE IN WATER TEMPARTURE AS WE PROCEED NORTH FROM THE GULF OF MEXICO / AMERICA. WE HAVE A RELATIVELY HIGH LEVEL OF CONFIDENCE IN BEING ABLE TO KEEP A 0 DISCHARGE RATE HOWEVER WE DO HAVE TO MAINTAIN PRESSURE ON THE OIL TO AVOID WATER INGRESS. GIVEN THIS WE HAVE MADE ARRANGEMENTS TO PROCURE A BOOM THROUGHOUT OUR PORT CALL. WORST CASE LOSS WE HAVE OBSERVED IN THE LAST WEEK HAS BEEN 10L / DAY WITH THE THRUSTER RUNNING OR OPERATING, HOWEVER AS PREVIOUSLY STATED WE HAVE OBSERVED ZERO LOSS IN THE LAST COUPLE OF DAYS.

IT IS BELIEVED THAT THE PASSENGER TRAIN RESPONSIBLE WAS THE 1219 NUMBER 4 TRAIN GOING FROM NEW LOTS TO WOODLAWN. AS A RESULT OF THIS INCIDENT THE NUMBER 4 TRACK NORTHBOUND WAS CLOSED AND REMAINS CLOSED. THIS EVENT DID NOT OCCUR AS A RESULT OF A BRAKE FAILURE INCIDENT AND EMPLOYEES ON THE TRAIN WILL BE DRUG AND ALCOHOL TESTED. THE TRAIN AND TRACK SPEED WERE UNKNOWN TO THE CALLER AND THIS DID NOT OCCUR AT A GRADE CROSSING.
